standard.title: Seek, give or deny permission
standard.description: practise strategies they can use when they need to seek, give or deny permission respectfully
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored how to seek, give or deny permission respectfully when sharing possessions or personal space (AC9HPFP04).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students practise strategies for seeking, giving or denying permission respectfully.

nodes.label: Seeking, giving and refusing consent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can practise strategies for giving or refusing consent, including verbal and non-verbal approaches.
nodes.minimum_width: In a practised scenario, use at least one verbal strategy (e.g. saying yes or no assertively) and one non-verbal cue or gesture to give or refuse consent.
nodes.typical_width: Practise a range of strategies for seeking, giving and denying permission — including assertive verbal responses, body cues, and gestures — across a variety of situations.
wider: Practise saying no to inappropriate touching and other boundary violations using assertive language and non-verbal cues
Explore situations where non-verbal cues alone may not be sufficient and discuss when verbal communication is essential
Compare how permission strategies are used in different contexts (sharing equipment, physical contact, personal space) and identify which strategies are most effective in each
nodes.hinge_reason: Practising assertive verbal and non-verbal permission strategies is the foundational capability of this descriptor. Students who lack a practised, embodied set of responses cannot apply them confidently in real situations — which is the safety concern underpinning this standard.

response_modes.reason: These strategies must be rehearsed until automatic — not just understood conceptually. Regular role-play practice across varied scenarios builds the fluency required for confident real-world application.

success_criteria: Uses at least one verbal strategy to give or refuse consent in a practised scenario
Uses at least one non-verbal cue or gesture to communicate consent or refusal

nodes.label: Fair and respectful interaction regardless of difference
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can practise ways to interact with others in a fair and respectful way in play and other activities, regardless of differences in gender, abilities, race or personality.
nodes.minimum_width: In a play or activity context, demonstrate at least one fair and respectful interaction with a person who is different from themselves; describe what they did.
nodes.typical_width: Practise fair and respectful interaction across a range of play and activity contexts involving diverse peers; explain how respecting difference contributes to the activity being positive for everyone.
wider: Compare how the same respectful interaction strategy works with peers of different abilities, genders, or backgrounds
Explore scenarios where differences in personality or preferences create friction in activities, and practise strategies for managing these respectfully
Discuss how respecting difference in physical activities connects to the fair-play principles students have explored in movement contexts

response_modes.reason: Respectful interaction across different types of difference requires practice in varied contexts. Explicitly vary peer configurations (different abilities, genders, personalities) in activity tasks so students practise the full range of the descriptor.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Practising respectful interaction across different dimensions of difference (gender, ability, race, personality) builds more robust and transferable social competence than practising with homogeneous groups.
success_criteria: Demonstrates a fair and respectful interaction with a peer who is different from themselves
Can describe what they did to interact respectfully
